subject.title: SecretRef credentials travel as plaintext through the model-call chain after resolution

question: Should OpenClaw adopt the process-local sentinel and egress-injection design for SecretRef-managed model credentials after the linked PR fixes its local-service probe gap, or require a narrower staged hardening plan first?
rationale: The plaintext propagation is source-supported, but the remedy changes cross-cutting credential handling and provider adapter behavior under a security-sensitive boundary.

options.title: Fix probe boundary and continue
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102009 as the canonical fix candidate once local-service health probes are sentinel-safe, then require security and compatibility review before merge.

options.title: Stage smaller hardening
options.body: Ask for a narrower first PR such as exact-value redaction plus guarded-fetch convergence, leaving full sentinels for a follow-up design.

options.title: Keep current boundary for now
options.body: Accept the documented same-process plaintext limitation for model credentials until a broader broker or plugin API design is approved.

recommendation.title: Fix probe boundary and continue
recommendation.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102009 as the canonical fix candidate once local-service health probes are sentinel-safe, then require security and compatibility review before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest current history around SecretRef and auth-profile resolution, which is the first security boundary this decision changes.
